CS No. 703/2023 CNR No. DLET01-013884-2023 In the matter of :-
Shri Sunil Sharma,
S/o Late Shri K.C. Sharma,
R/o 96/2, Patparganj Village,
Near Mayur Vihar, Phase-I,
Delhi-110091.
 .....Plaintiff  Versus Ms. Mamta,
D/o Shri Mohan Das,
R/o MB 169, 3rd Floor,
Flat Park Side, Master Block,
Shakarpur, Delhi-110092.
 .....Defendant Date of Institution : 22.12.2023 Date of Reserving Judgment : 26.02.2026 Date of Decision : 06.03.2026  JUDGMENT 1.

By way of instant suit, the plaintiff is seeking eviction of defendant from the tenanted premises,
i.e., 2BHK on Third Floor at Property bearing No. MB 169, 3 rd Floor, Flat Park Side, Master Block,
Shakarpur, Delhi-110092 (hereinafter Sunil Sharma Vs. Mamta referred to as the suit property),
along with recovery of arrears of rent, mesne profits and permanent injunction.

2. Briefly stated facts as disclosed in the plaint are the plaintiff is the absolute owner/landlord of the suit property, which was let out to the defendant at monthly rent of Rs.14,000/- for a period of 11 months, commencing from 01.12.2022 for residential purpose.
No written rent agreement was executed between the parties, hence, the tenancy was oral.
It is alleged that the defendant had only paid rent for the month of December, 2022 and did not pay any rent w.e.f. 01.01.2023.

When the plaintiff asked the defendant to pay the rent due upon her, the defendant lodged a false FIR No.
108/23, PS Shakarpur, U/s 376/354B/506 IPC in order to extort money from the plaintiff.

It is stated that the friend of the plaintiff namely Ms. Sunita Shahi had also lodged an FIR No. 128/23,
PS Shakarpur, U/s 388/120B IPC against the defendant and her associates.
The plaintiff terminated the tenancy of the defendant vide legal notice, dated 20.10.2023.
The defendant neither replied to the notice nor handed over the possession of the suit property.

The plaintiff claims that the defendant is liable to pay arrears of rent to the tune of Rs.1,54,000/- w.e.f. 01.01.2023 to Sunil Sharma Vs. Mamta 30.11.2023 and is further liable to pay mesne profits @ Rs.1,000/- per day w.e.f.
27.10.2023 to 27.11.2023 till its realization.

creation of third party interest, alienation or parting with possession of the suit property has also been made.
3. Due service of summons was made upon the defendant as recorded by the Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 26.09.2024.
However, when none appeared for the defendant nor any written statement was filed, the defence of the defendant was struck off by Ld. Predecessor.
4. After striking off the defence of defendant, Ld. Predecessor, vide order dated 26.09.2024, framed following issues:-
( 1) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the decree of ejectment, as prayed for in the prayer clause A. of the plaint?

OPP. 
(2) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the decree for Rs.1,54,000/- as claimed B. in the prayer clause of the plaint?

OPP. 
(3) To what amount of damages, the plaintiff is entitled for and if so, at what rate and for what period?

OPP. 
Sunil Sharma Vs. Mamta (4) Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the decree for injunction, as claimed in prayer clause D. of the plaint?
OPP. (5) Relief.

5. In support of his claim, the plaintiff examined himself as PW1, Sh. Mahesh Babu, Record Keeper,
Sub-Registrar VIII- A, as PW2 and Head Constable Kapil from PS Shakarpur as PW3.
6. The plaintiff, Sh. Sunil Sharma stepped into the witness box as PW1 and tendered his affidavit of evidence as Ex.PW1/1.

He relied upon the documents, i.e., site plan as Ex.PW1/A; sale deed, dated 01.10.2024 of the suit property as Ex.PW1/B; legal notice, dated 20.10.2023 as Ex.PW1/C; postal receipt as Ex.PW1/D; and FIR No. 108/23 and 128/23, both of PS Shakarpur, as Mark A and Mark B respectively.
7. PW2/Sh. Mahesh Babu, Record Keeper, Sub-Registrar VIII-A, proved the sale deed, dated 07.10.2025 executed in favour of plaintiff Ex.PW2/A (colly.).

He also proved the authority letter executed in his favour as Ex.PW2/B.
8.

PW3/HC Kapil was also a summoned witness, who had Sunil Sharma Vs. Mamta brought the summoned record, i.e., FIR No. 108/23 lodged by defendant against the plaintiff under Section 376/506 IPC, PS Shakarpur and also FIR No. 128/23, U/s 388/120B IPC lodged by Ms. Sunita Shahi against Madhu Aggarwal and the defendant.
He proved the said FIRs as Ex.PW3/A and Ex.PW3/B respectively.
9. No cross-examination of the aforesaid witnesses was conducted as the defence of the defendant had already been struck off by Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 26.09.2024.
Thereafter, the plaintiff closed his evidence and the matter was listed for final arguments.

sentences.text: 10. Submissions advanced by Ld. Counsel for plaintiff have been heard and record perused.
None appeared on behalf of defendant to address arguments.

11. Issue-wise findings are as under:-
ISSUE No.1- "Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the decree of ejectment, as prayed for in the prayer clause A. of the plaint?"
12.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the plaintiff.

In a Sunil Sharma Vs. Mamta civil suit for possession, the plaintiff has to prove the following :-
(a) The rent was more than Rs.3,500/- per month i.e. the tenancy was beyond the ambit of the Delhi Rent Control Act.
(b) The tenancy has been validly terminated.
(c) Needless to say, the existence of landlord and tenant relationship.
13. The plaintiff/PW1 has categorical deposed that he is the owner of the suit property which he had let out to the defendant at monthly rent of Rs.14,000/- on 01.12.2022.
The testimony of plaintiff has remained unrebutted and uncontroverted and there is no reason to disbelieve the same.

Moreover,
the defendant in FIR Ex.PW3/A has admitted that she is a tenant of the plaintiff.
Thus, the existence of jural relationship of landlord-tenant between the parties stands duly proved.

The tenancy was for a period of 11 months, commencing from 01.12.2022, so it automatically stood terminated by efflux of time on 31.10.2023, however, to be not in a precarious position, the plaintiff also served legal notice, dated 20.10.2023 upon the defendant thereby, terminating the tenancy.

Filing of the present suit for eviction per se, is also sufficient notice of termination of tenancy Sunil Sharma Vs. Mamta (reference may be made to the judgement titled as Jeevan Diesel & Electrical Vs. Jasbir Singh Chadha, 185 (2011) DLT 402).
14.

sentences.text: In view of above, the Court is of the opinion that the plaintiff has established the essential ingredients for recovery of possession of the suit property.
15. Issue No.1 is, accordingly, decided in favour of plaintiff and against the defendant.
Issue No.2 "Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the decree for Rs.1,54,000/- as claimed B. in the prayer clause of the plaint?"
16. The onus to prove this issue was upon the plaintiff.
The plaintiff has averred that the defendant failed to pay the monthly rent w.e.f. January, 2023.

sentences.text: It is settled law that when the plaintiff/landlord alleges non-payment of rent, the onus lies upon the defendant/tenant to prove that he has paid the rent.

It has been held in Sukhanand Vs. IVth Additional District Judge, Bulendshahar & ors., 1994 (2) RCR (Rent) 408 that the onus to show Sunil Sharma Vs. Mamta payment of rent lies on the tenant and oral testimony of tenant in regard to the payment of rent claiming discharge of liability in this regard cannot be admitted to be worth reliance at all.
18.

entities.text: Sukhanand Vs. IVth Additional District Judge, Bulendshahar & ors., 1994 (2) RCR (Rent) 408
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case, the defendant has not chosen to contest the case and has not been able to prove that she had made regular payment of rent to the plaintiff.

In the absence of any evidence on record regarding payment of rent being adduced by the defendant, the Court is left with no option,
but to accept the unchallenged testimony of plaintiff/PW1 qua non-payment of rent w.e.f.
01.01.2023.

Accordingly, the plaintiff is held entitled to recover arrears of rent @ 14,000/- pm w.e.f.
01.01.2023 till 31.10.2023.
19.
Issue No.2 is also decided in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant.
Issue No.3 "To what amount of damages, the plaintiff is entitled for and if so, at what rate and for what period?"
20. The plaintiff has also claimed mesne profits / damages at the rate of Rs.30,000/- per month.
Mesne profits is nothing, Sunil Sharma Vs. Mamta but the damages which the erstwhile tenant has to pay after determination of lease.
The landlord has to be compensated for the loss caused, because he is denied and deprived of the possession of the property.
21. The question of damages automatically comes to the fora as from 01.11.2023, the tenancy does not subsist and after 01.11.2023, the defendant had no permission for occupation of the suit property.
22. The plaintiff has not led any cogent evidence as to what rental the suit property would have fetched during the pendency of the present suit.

The plaintiff has not examined any person who was well versed with the rentals prevailing in the area in which the suit property is situated nor the record from Sub Registrar's office has been summoned so that the lease deeds executed during the contemporaneous period could have been brought on record.

The mesne profits are accordingly awarded @ Rs. 14,000/- per month with effect from 01.11.2023 till handing over the vacant and peaceful possession of the suit property, subject to filing of appropriate court fees on record.
Sunil Sharma Vs. Mamta 23.
Issue No.3 is decided in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant.
Issue No.4 "Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the decree for injunction, as claimed in prayer clause D. of the plaint?"

sentences.text: A restraint order with respect to creation of third party interest has also been prayed for.
The plaintiff is the owner of the suit property whereas the defendant is a tenant whose tenancy has been validly terminated.
The defendant has no right, title or interest qua the suit property, hence, plaintiff is entitled to the relief of permanent injunction as well.
25. Consequently, this issue No.4 is decided in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant.

RELIEF:-
26.

In view of the foregoing reasons and discussion, the suit of the plaintiff is decreed in following terms:-
1.

The plaintiff is entitled to recover possession of the suit property, i.e., Property bearing No. MB 169, 3rd Floor, Flat Park Side, Master Block, Shakarpur,
Delhi-110092.
2. The plaintiff is entitled to recover arrears of rent @ Sunil Sharma Vs. Mamta Rs.14,000/-pm w.e.f. 01.01.2023 till 31.10.2023, thus, totaling to an amount of Rs.1,40,000/-.

3. The plaintiff is further held entitled to mesne profits @ Rs. 14,000/- per month with effect from 01.11.2023 till handing over the vacant and peaceful possession of the suit property, subject to filing of appropriate court fees on record.
4. The plaintiff is further entitled to decree of permanent injunction.
The defendant is restrained from selling, transferring, alienating, parting with possession or creating any third party interest in the suit property.
5. Cost of the suit is also awarded in favour of the plaintiff.
27. Decree sheet shall be prepared accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
Announced in the open Court on 06.03.2026.
(Shuchi Laler) District Judge-02, East District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi.
